content.title: About
content.content: Sockeye salmon is a species of wild Pacific salmon that migrates from the ocean to freshwater rivers to spawn. It is harvested from its natural habitat without farm feeding and sold raw. The flesh is bright orange, firm, and has a rich, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sockeye is one of the most valuable salmon species for commercial fisheries.
The orange color comes from astaxanthin, a natural carotenoid pigment.
Wild sockeye travel up to 3,000 km from the ocean to inland rivers to spawn.
The typical harvest season in North America runs from June to August.
Raw sockeye is a popular choice for sushi and sashimi because of its firm texture.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Sockeye provides EPA and DHA, which support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: About 20 g of complete protein per 100 g serving helps build and repair body tissues.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and contributes to immune function.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Astaxanthin in sockeye helps protect the retina from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Parasite risk
items.content: Raw fish may harbor parasites; freezing at –20 °C for at least 7 days reduces this risk.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to fish can experience severe reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Sockeye generally has low mercury, but pregnant women and children should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sockeye is commonly served as sashimi, sushi, tartare, or lightly marinated in soy sauce. It can be quickly grilled or baked, but many prefer it raw to preserve its delicate flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh sockeye in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, tightly sealed, and use within 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Before consumption, check for off‑odors or discoloration, which indicate spoilage.
